overall: The AG found the Northborough Board of Selectmen violated the Open Meeting Law by posting a September 12 notice that omitted appointee names and the bargaining union, and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the September 12 meeting notice did not name the candidates for appointment to library trustees, scholarship committee, and registrars.
allegations.key_passage: a meeting notice must include on the notice itself the level of specificity that the Open Meeting Law requires; we do not review the contents of an accompanying meeting packet.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the executive session on collective bargaining strategy did not identify the union whose contract was discussed.
allegations.key_passage: When convening in executive session pursuant to Purpose 3, a public body must identify the collective bargaining unit with whom it will be negotiating, if doing so will not compromise the lawful purpose for secrecy.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Board that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
